angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 257,409 km at 110.48 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.0513 +/- 0.0324 mas (same row, RUWE 1.02): 110.48 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.37 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-242 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract): 257,409 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.38 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-242 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3459 +/- 65 K from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-242 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-242 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-242.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.881, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
